findings.issue_text: Public group members page is hard-capped at server default limit of 50 but the group-members route/template has no pagination controls, so groups with >50 members silently show only the first 50 with no way to see the rest
totalPages calculation Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 overcounts when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100 users / 50 reports 3 pages); should be Math.ceil(user_count / limit)

next action clamps offset to Math.min(offset + limit, user_count), so on the last full page boundary the next click sets offset == user_count and fetches an empty member page, landing the user on a blank page

groups_controller.rb#members passes limit and offset straight to SQL with no clamping: negative values raise ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid 500 and uncapped limit allows arbitrarily large queries on a public unauthenticated endpoint (DoS vector)

admin/groups_controller.rb#remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id) which destroys the association row directly, bypassing Group#remove/GroupUser callbacks like primary-group/title cleanup and derived counters
add_members splits usernames on ',' without stripping whitespace, so 'bob, alice' fails to find ' alice'; it also returns success even when no usernames match existing users (silent no-op)

admin groups controller specs hard-code id: 1/group_id: 1 assuming seeded automatic group data; if the seed is missing or ids shift, Group.find(1) raises RecordNotFound and tests break; should use Fabricate(:group, automatic: true)

In group_member.hbs, the rendering context inside the group-member itemView is the member item, so {{#unless automatic}} doesn't resolve to the group's automatic flag; the remove link renders for automatic groups too and clicking gets a 422; automatic needs to be passed explicitly
No spec covers the new pagination envelope (meta.total/limit/offset) or that pagination now applies to non-automatic groups, which is a behavior change for existing API consumers

admin groups create action only reads name and visible but ignores alias_level sent by the client's asJSON(), so a newly created group always gets the default alias level, silently dropping the admin's selection

Rapid pagination clicks in next/previous fire overlapping findMembers() requests with no cancellation or sequence guard, so out-of-order responses can leave offset/members inconsistent with the displayed page
The admin get "users" endpoint is removed outright from config/routes.rb with no deprecation or replacement, breaking existing API/plugin consumers of that route

admin_group_route.js and group-members.js.es6 setupController fire model.findMembers() but don't return/handle its promise, so route loading state is skipped and request failures are silently swallowed (stale/empty member list with no error)

The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' spec issues xhr :put although the action/route is DELETE; it passes only because controller specs invoke the action directly, masking a routing mismatch

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public group members page is hard-capped at server default limit of 50 but the group-members route/template has no pagination controls, so groups with >50 members silently show only the first 50 with no way to see the rest

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the server now always applies pagination with `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `members = ...limit(limit).offset(offset)`, returning only that slice plus `meta.total/limit/offset`. On the client, `group-members` route now does `controller.set("model", model); model.findMembers();` and the template `group/members.hbs` iterates `{{#each m in members}}`, where `members` is set by `Group#findMembers` from the paginated response. However, unlike the admin group UI, the public `group/members` template/route changes add no next/previous actions or other pagination controls, so with default `offset=0` only the first 50 members are shown and there is no UI path to request subsequent pages. This is a real regression versus the previous server behavior for non-automatic groups (no limit).

adjudication_records.issue_text: groups_controller.rb#members passes limit and offset straight to SQL with no clamping: negative values raise ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid 500 and uncapped limit allows arbitrarily large queries on a public unauthenticated endpoint (DoS vector)

adjudication.rationale: In app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members, the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then uses them directly in `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no validation or clamping. This allows negative values (e.g., `offset = -5`) to reach SQL; in PostgreSQL, negative OFFSET raises an error, producing a 500. It also allows arbitrarily large `limit` values, which can trigger very large queries. The endpoint is in GroupsController (not admin) and only guarded by `guardian.ensure_can_see!(group)`, so for visible groups it can be hit unauthenticated, making the large-limit query a plausible DoS vector. The problem is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin/groups_controller.rb#remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id) which destroys the association row directly, bypassing Group#remove/GroupUser callbacks like primary-group/title cleanup and derived counters

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member` using `group.users.delete(user_id)` instead of the previously-used `group.remove(user)` pattern (seen in the removed `update_patch`). However, the finding’s core claim—that this *bypasses* important `Group#remove` / `GroupUser` callbacks (primary-group/title cleanup, counter maintenance, etc.)—is not verifiable from the diff because the implementations of `Group#remove`, the `has_many` association type, and any join-model callbacks are not shown. If `Group#remove` is just a thin wrapper around `users.delete`, then there is no bug. So the asserted callback-bypass defect is speculative given only this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members splits usernames on ',' without stripping whitespace, so 'bob, alice' fails to find ' alice'; it also returns success even when no usernames match existing users (silent no-op)

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the code does `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` and then calls `User.find_by_username(username)` without trimming. This means inputs like "bob, alice" will look up " alice" (leading space) and fail to match an existing user, so the whitespace handling issue is a real defect visible in the diff. The second claim (returning success even when no usernames match) is also behavior present (it will still `group.save` and render success_json even if nothing was added), though it may be consistent with prior behavior (older specs explicitly allowed silent success for non-existent users).

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin groups controller specs hard-code id: 1/group_id: 1 assuming seeded automatic group data; if the seed is missing or ids shift, Group.find(1) raises RecordNotFound and tests break; should use Fabricate(:group, automatic: true)

adjudication.rationale:
The updated specs introduce hard-coded references to `id: 1` / `group_id: 1` for “automatic group” behavior:
- `.update` spec: `xhr :put, :update, id: 1, ...` then `Group.find(1)`
- `.add_members` spec: `xhr :put, :add_members, group_id: 1, ...` expecting 422
These tests assume that group with ID 1 exists in the test DB and is automatic. That is not guaranteed by anything shown in the diff; if the seeded/bootstrapped groups aren’t present or IDs differ, `Group.find(1)` will raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` and the specs will fail. Using `Fabricate(:group, automatic: true)` (or looking up by name) would avoid this brittleness.

No spec covers the new pagination envelope (meta.total/limit/offset) or that pagination now applies to non-automatic groups, which is a behavior change for existing API consumers

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (a bare array response) to returning an object with `{ members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }`, and it now applies `limit/offset` for all groups (previously only for `group.automatic?`). That is a concrete, breaking response-shape/behavior change visible in the diff. The only spec file modified is `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb`, and no new/updated spec for `GroupsController#members` (or for the new `meta` envelope / pagination behavior) is added in this diff, so the change isn’t covered by tests here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin groups create action only reads name and visible but ignores alias_level sent by the client's asJSON(), so a newly created group always gets the default alias level, silently dropping the admin's selection

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the diff, the client’s `Discourse.Group#asJSON()` includes `alias_level` (and the group form binds `alias_level` via the combo-box), and `create()` POSTs `data: this.asJSON()` to `/admin/groups`. However, `Admin::GroupsController#create` only sets `group.name` and `group.visible` and never reads/assigns `params[:alias_level]`. Therefore the selected alias level is silently ignored on creation and the new group will use the model default alias_level instead.

The admin get "users" endpoint is removed outright from config/routes.rb with no deprecation or replacement, breaking existing API/plugin consumers of that route

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `get "users"` route under the admin groups resource in `config/routes.rb` and replaces it with `put "members"` and `delete "members"`. So the old endpoint is indeed gone. However, the finding’s claim that this is removed “with no … replacement” is not accurate in the context of the diff: there are new admin `members` endpoints intended to cover group membership changes, and the UI/model code has been updated to use them. The assertion that it “break[s] existing API/plugin consumers” is also speculative (not verifiable from the diff alone).
